A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same K-Sort Arena paper with readable main text and complete appendices. Sections, equations, tables and figures can be matched reliably across the localized additions and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original ranking simulations in Section 4 and crowdsourced image/video model evaluations in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds a voting-time study involving ten trained participants in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The K-wise comparison procedure, probabilistic capability model, Bayesian updates, UCB matchmaking and pivot-selection rule remain unchanged. Appendix F evaluates the existing approach.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds short- and long-prompt scenarios for evaluating human voting effort and reports using DiffusionDB for long prompts. The existing image/video tasks and MS COCO/WebVid prompt coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Table 1 and Figures 3–6 remains unchanged, including ELO and TrueSkill-style matchmaking. The added timing study varies K and prompt complexity without introducing another comparison algorithm.

E3.justification: The added study measures prompt-reading and image-voting time for ten trained participants at K=2, 4 and 6, using approximately 20-token and 120-token prompts. Existing simulation and crowdsourcing protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds an analysis of how human effort depends on K and prompt complexity. This supplements v1's K-sensitivity analysis of simulated ranking convergence in Figure 4; the existing noise, matchmaking and pivot analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Existing uncertainty displays, including the model means and standard deviations in Figures 7–8, are retained. The new timing study introduces no reported error bars, confidence intervals, repeated-trial counts or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figure 10 adds timing results, including approximately 13 seconds at K=2 versus 16 seconds at K=4 for short prompts. Existing results remain unchanged, including Table 1's 11,692 comparisons for ELO versus 716 for K-Sort Arena.

T1.justification: Section 3 and Appendices A–B retain the same mathematical definitions, Bayesian-update derivations and UCB regret argument. No formal assumption, result or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient, robust K-wise evaluation and 16.3-fold faster convergence than ELO. The new study supplies supporting evidence without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix F interprets the additional effort at K=4 as acceptable and argues that long prompts shift cognitive effort toward comprehension, reducing the relative cost of image selection. These interpretations extend the existing convergence-based discussion.

D1.justification: Implementation parameters, the Gradio/ZeroGPU/Replicate setup, model documentation and access links remain unchanged. Appendix F adds evaluation conditions but no new implementation details, processing instructions or code/data access information.

R1.justification: Section 2, the 57 bibliographic entries and the positioning against earlier evaluation systems remain unchanged. DiffusionDB is introduced as a study data source without revising the related-work discussion.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short User Behavior Analysis appendix, moves and expands the acknowledgements, and changes Dongrong Fu's displayed name to Dongrong Joe Fu. The main scientific narrative is otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds timing Figure 10, enlarges Figure 9 and retains the interface figure as Figure 11. The appendix and references reflow, and printed page numbers are removed; existing result tables and plots are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix F and Figure 10 add direct evidence about per-vote human effort, which v1's convergence simulations did not measure. This modestly strengthens the practical motivation for K-wise voting. The ten-participant study lacks trial-count, aggregation and variability details, limiting its evidential strength; the existing technical content and results are preserved.
